correctness_finding_at_release.effect: Best family F4 for vector 165876523 moved from (46.53, -125.75) to (46.53, -7.19) -- rotated toward the Stonehenge training anchor, landing 648.8 km away, consistent with its 5.69-degree sealed residual. Calibration is now non-cosmetic.

negative_results: NULL RESULT: even with the fit correctly applied, the coordinate system does NOT decode 165876523 to Stonehenge. The best family reproduces the training anchor only to ~649 km; the other retained families are 7,431 and 8,948 km away. A single fitted azimuth (1 DOF) cannot align two arbitrary anchor directions (4 scalar constraints); this is structural, not a bug.

The application therefore renders a CANDIDATE_ALIAS_SET with per-family uncertainty and an agreement/disagreement surface -- a pin or region always, never a bare refusal, and never invented precision.
A guard test refuses any future family placement within 100 km of the training anchor as a probable overfit / famous-place reward.

claims.statement: A candidate pin is a CALIBRATED_CANDIDATE SOFTWARE_RESULT under a declared, frozen calibration; it is not a measured fact.
The two sealed training anchors do not select a mapping that places the source vectors at their claimed Earth locations.
